html:
Mencius was a Chinese philosopher of the Warring States period, the most important follower of Confucius. Chinese tradition calls him the "Second Sage".

He studied with pupils of Confucius's grandson and spent much of his life travelling between the courts of rival states, giving advice that kings rarely took. His sayings and debates were collected in the book Mencius.

His key ideas:

  • Human nature is good. Everyone has "sprouts" of kindness, shame, respect and a sense of right and wrong, which need to be grown, as a farmer tends his crops.
  • A ruler should govern by kindness and care for the people's livelihood.
  • A ruler who cruelly oppresses the people loses the Mandate of Heaven, and may rightly be overthrown.

He argued against the followers of Mozi, and the later thinker Xunzi answered him by saying human nature is bad. In the Song dynasty, Zhu Xi made Mencius one of the Four Books that every student had to learn for the examinations.
sum: Mencius was a Chinese philosopher of the Warring States period, the most important follower of Confucius. Chinese tradition calls him the "Second Sage".
